items.title: Iran war derailed talks to claw back billions in tax credits paid to miners
items.description: Billions in tax credits are paid to coal miners every year. Ministers discussed clawing back some of that money in the May federal budget, but the Iran war has pushed out those talks.

items.title: The BHP files reveal a big problem facing the mining giant
items.description: For a company that prides itself on digging out the metals for the world's clean energy future, saying nothing about its own clean energy future is not an option.

items.title: Live: Jobseeker services to get first overhaul in 30 years
items.description: Employment Minister Amanda Rishworth will today announce major changes to Australia's unemployment system, which currently supports more than 1 million jobseekers. Follow live.

items.title: Fidel Castro's daughter fled his regime, and has a warning for the US
items.description: Fidel Castro's daughter says the US has failed to find a way to deal with Cuba for decades. But she tells the ABC that the Trump administration has a difference that could spell the end of the regime she fled.

items.title: Women and children linked to ISIS spend first night back in Australia
items.description: A group of so-called ISIS brides who left the notorious al-Roj camp in Syria last week have spent their first night home in Australia.

items.title: Woman forced out of home as mould grows after insurer repairs roof
items.description: Lily lodged an insurance claim with her provider GIO Suncorp after a truck ran through her street's power lines. Nearly a decade later, she has been forced out of her home.

items.title: Iran calls latest US strikes 'bad faith' sign as internet slowly restored
items.description: Iran has denounced US strikes in the country's south as a sign of "bad faith and unreliability" as negotiations toward a possible deal to end the war continue.

items.title: Australian students record worst tech literacy results on record
items.description: Australian students have recorded their worst-ever results in national tests that measure digital literacy, with just 37 per cent of year 10 students and 50 per cent of year 6 students assessed as proficient.

items.title: Why drones fell from the sky during Sydney's Vivid light show
items.description: The company behind the drone shows at Sydney's Vivid festival said spectators were not at risk when almost 90 unmanned aircraft fell from the sky during a display on Monday night.

items.title: Rain brings potential 'opportunities' in renewed search for Gus Lamont, police say
items.description: Eight months since Gus Lamont was reported missing, police have again returned to search Oak Park Station as part of an ongoing investigations into the four-year-old's disappearance.

items.title: At least 11 dead as Europe bakes in unprecedented heatwave
items.description: The British capital's previous hottest May day was set only one day prior, when the mercury topped 33.5C.

items.title: Scott's sacking gives Essendon another chance to step out of Hird's shadow
items.description: Essendon finds itself at a clear demarcation point after sacking Brad Scott as the shadow of James Hird once again looms large over the troubled club.

items.title: Student says WA school closed by toxic baits had been overrun by mice
items.description: A year 12 student at the WA College of Agriculture Morawa says there were fears of "cooking" mice in the heating system before the mistaken deployment of toxic baits shut the school down.

items.title: BP removes chair over 'serious concerns' about conduct
items.description: The BBC reported Albert Manifold's departure followed concerns about "bullying" and his "overbearing" behaviour.

items.title: Next steps when you get 'life-altering' ancestry DNA test results
items.description: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing kits are often given as gifts or purchased "as a bit of fun", which means people often aren't prepared to discover unexpected parents, siblings and other relatives.

items.title: Why Blak Douglas won't enter the Archibald Prize again
items.description: The acclaimed Dunghutti artist is using his latest exhibition to challenge perceptions of Aboriginal art and the systemic issues creatives face in Australia.

items.title: More or Less quiz: We need you to rank five State of Origin greats
items.description: If you think you know your stuff when it comes to State of Origin, here's your chance to prove it.

items.title: Department accused of 'poor decision making' over $6.2m helmet rollout
items.description: Queensland's fire minister has intervened following tensions between the firefighter union and department.

items.title: Complaint lodged with Canada's privacy commissioner over Australian court breach
items.description: Litigants in at least 146 court matters were potentially involved in a data breach that is now the subject of a formal complaint with the privacy commissioner in Canada, Senate estimates has been told.

items.title: Report warns AI boom could keep Australia using coal and gas for longer
items.description: A new report concludes the AI-fuelled surge of power-hungry data centres across Australia is jeopardising the country's energy transition.

items.title: Live: Westpac fined $26m for 'grossly negligent' conduct
items.description: The Federal Court imposes a $26 million fine on Westpac for failing to respond quickly to customers facing financial hardship. Follow live.

items.title: 'Can't put it into words': Origin star's mum reveals heartbreaking call
items.description: Cameron Munster's mum reveals the heartbreaking call she had to make before her superstar son led Queensland to victory days after the shock death of his dad.

items.title: 'Kidding ourselves': Daley whacks talk of Cleary's losing Origin record
items.description: NSW coach Laurie Daley says the responsibility does not solely rest on the shoulders of his star No.7 ahead of this year's State of Origin campaign.

items.title: The NSW Blues made a 'tough' selection call, so will the Wallabies
items.description: Just as NSW Blues coach Laurie Daley had a difficult selection decision to make, Joe Schmidt may be thinking long and hard about one position in the Wallabies' back line for July's Nations Championship Tests.

items.title: Two prospective Whyalla steelworks buyers remain, as sale reaches 'final stages'
items.description: The federal and state governments have reduced the number of bidders for the financially stricken Whyalla steelworks from five to two.
